origin.rerun: for n in $(gh api 'repos/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/pulls?state=open&per_page=60' --jq '.[].number'); do sha=$(gh api repos/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/pulls/$n --jq .head.sha); c=$(gh api "repos/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" --jq '[.check_runs[]|select(.name=="pytest-run")]|length'); [ "$c" = 0 ] && echo "$n no pytest-run on $sha"; done  # any line = a PR whose required checks never started

what: REQUIRED CI SOMETIMES NEVER STARTS ON A PR HEAD. MEASURED 2026-10-07: #16974 (head d736c609b) and #16980 (head f11a43fe2) had only push-triggered runs (armed-branch-push-watch, phone-executor-apk) and no pytest-collect / pytest-run / guards check-runs 20+ min after the push, while sibling PRs pushed the same minute got all three; both heads were a second 'landing: hold' fix commit pushed shortly after the PR opened; both PRs were opened by the user token, not by a workflow (so the GITHUB_TOKEN no-trigger rule is NOT the cause). The manager dispatched the three workflows by workflow_dispatch each time. Branch protection would leave such a PR unmergeable forever; the manager's merge watchers reported one of them GREEN on zero pending checks (fixed: a GREEN now requires the three required checks PRESENT). Question for a lane: what is the trigger-side cause (pull_request synchronize dropped? the opened+synchronize concurrency group cancelling and deleting the pending run? a paths filter?) and what mechanical backstop re-dispatches required checks for a PR head that has none after N minutes (schedule-keeper-style, on push to main).
